text:
claire: quick follow-up from today's architecture sync. proposing a compact 'handoff gateway' (HGW) that removes the need for a persistent per-tenant sidecar in hosted mode. HGW would perform capability negotiation + a short-lived handoff descriptor, then either create a TCP tunnel (fast path) or act as an inspect-proxy (audit path). dropping questions on probe semantics, eviction handling, and private-tenant opt-out.

jon: big +1 on avoiding per-tenant sidecars. main question: how do we guarantee isolation with a multitenant HGW?

claire: HGW will be AZ-local, stateless w.r.t long-lived secrets, and will only mint ephemeral handoff descriptors (opaque, PoP-signed tokens). runtimes enforce tenant isolation and network policies. HGW never stores model payloads to disk.

ali: opt-out for private control-planes is critical. we can add a tiny manifest toggle but it must be optional and default to "auto" so older private installs are unaffected.

sam: perf note: we should support two clearly documented modes: "tunnel" (negotiate -> direct TCP stream) and "proxy" (full application-layer proxying). default to tunnel for streaming endpoints. document latency budgets for each.

jon: eviction mid-stream is scary. what does graceful handoff look like if a runtime preempts a tenant?

claire: propose a small structured pre-close frame runtime can emit: STREAM_EVICT {resume_hint: "opaque", reason: "quota"}. client SDKs treat STREAM_EVICT as a resume token hint. tokens must be PoP-signed and single-use. older runtimes that don't support it fall back to full restart.

ali: security: resume_hint must be short-lived (<=60s), single-use, and verifiable by control-plane. HGW should validate format on handshake but must not persist tokens. add replay-detection telemetry.

sam: failure modes & fallbacks: 1) client pin -> direct runtime (preferred for Dedicated/Private), 2) control-plane proxy (current hosted flow), 3) HGW. if HGW unhealthy, SDKs should try pinned direct; hosted non-pinned tenants get routed to fallback model variant. HGW should expose a circuit-breaker metric for SDKs to observe.

jon: what about quick recovery for interactive UX? reconnect+resume must be <250ms ideally. if we can't meet that, consider opt-in hedging (dual-write to standby runtime) as a paid feature for high-SLA tenants.

claire: agreed. hedging/dual-write is opt-in and billed; default remains single-writer to keep costs down. we'll add an explicit billing_tag in the handshake so runtime knows attribution when tunneling.

ali: probes: split probe endpoints: /health/runtime and /health/hgw. control-plane should prefer runtime health when deciding fallbacks. probes must respect tenant opt-out so private installs never show hosted HGW metrics by default.

ops-bot: infra task created: https://infra/board/hgw-canary  includes per-AZ canary plan, mTLS lifecycle, feature-flag gate, resume-token spec, and privacy audit checklist.

deploy-bot: checklist PR opened: https://infra/repo/hgw/PR-821  items: cert rotation, canary config, FF gate, dashboards, resume-token validator.

sam: tests I'll own: latency tunnel vs direct, STREAM_EVICT resume+reconnect, opt-out correctness (private installs), token replay attempt blocked, privacy audit proving no payloads persisted.

jon: add SLO targets in the RFC: median extra latency for tunnel <= 3ms within region, proxy path median <= 12ms. include metrics that trigger auto-fallback to direct route if HGW misses budget.

ali: manifest sketch (optional, tiny):

`runtime.handoff.use_hgw = "auto"  # values: auto|always|never`

and an optional baggage field: `runtime.handoff.billing_tag = "hosted:lite"` for attribution.

claire: perfect. I'll draft a compact RFC with sequence diagrams for tunnel/proxy, STREAM_EVICT token lifecycle, probe semantics, SLOs, canary & rollback plan, and a short ops runbook for cert rotation + kill-switch. posting in 24h for 72h review. thanks y'all :rocket:
